## An unsupervised result has no answers to test against

k-means and hierarchical clustering return groups for any table, and PCA returns
components for any table. A supervised model can be checked against held-out answers;
an unsupervised one has no answers to hold out. Three checks take their place, and
together they show whether a pattern is worth reporting and what kind of pattern it is.

This page puts the two-cluster result from [Clustering with k-means](clustering.qmd)
through all three, and then a second split that passes the first check and fails the
others.

{{< include ../../_snippets/simulated-data.qmd >}}

{{< include ../../_snippets/python-tabs-run.qmd >}}

## The idea

::: {.diagram}
![Three checks before reporting a pattern. Refit on bootstrap samples and see whether the same grouping comes back; look at where the stations sit between the two cluster centres, where real groups leave a gap and a gradient does not; and compare the grouping with a recorded variable that the method was never given.](img/pattern-checks.svg){fig-alt="Three cards side by side with a strip of definitions below. 1 Replication: three small bootstrap samples, each clustered into a blue and an orange group, give the same grouping, captioned the same grouping comes back in every sample. 2 Group or gradient: two small histograms of where stations sit between the two cluster centres, with a dashed boundary line half way; the upper one, labelled groups: a gap, has two humps and almost nothing at the boundary; the lower one, labelled gradient: no gap, is flat from end to end. 3 External check: a column of cluster points, three blue and three orange, each beside a recorded seabed label, hard for every blue point and soft for every orange one, captioned matches a variable the method was never given. The strip reads: bootstrap sample, sites drawn at random with replacement, each with all its stations; ARI, agreement of two groupings, pair by pair, 1 for identical and 0 for chance; recorded variable, measured separately and left out of the analysis."}
:::

1. **Replication.** Refit the clustering on many bootstrap samples and compare each new
   grouping with the original using the adjusted Rand index (ARI) from
   [Hierarchical clustering](beyond-k-means.qmd). A real pattern comes back.
2. **Group or gradient.** k-means cuts a gradient as readily as it finds a gap, and a
   steady gradient is cut in the same place every time, so it comes back too. Where the
   stations sit between the two centres tells the two apart: groups leave a gap at the
   boundary, a gradient does not.
3. **An external variable.** Compare the grouping with something recorded separately and
   left out of the analysis, such as the seabed type. Agreement with a variable the method
   never saw is the strongest evidence available.

## Worked example

### Sixty bootstrap samples give two answers

A **bootstrap sample**, from
[Random forests and boosting](../03-supervised-learning/forests-and-boosting.qmd), draws
rows at random with replacement. Stations at the same site are more alike than stations
from different sites, so here whole sites are drawn, as in
[Dependent data](../06-assumptions-limitations/dependent-data.qmd);
`group_bootstraps()` in rsample does this. k-means, with the recipe of
[Clustering with k-means](clustering.qmd), is refitted on each of 60 samples, and the
refitted model assigns every station of the survey to its nearest centre. Each grouping is
then compared with the original one, with the recorded seabed, and by how far apart in
depth its two clusters sit.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap
survey <- load_coastal_survey_clean()
community <- load_coastal_community()

stations <- community |>
  inner_join(dplyr::select(survey, station_id, site_id, depth_m, substrate),
             by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(bottom = if_else(substrate %in% c("rock", "gravel"), "hard", "soft"))

taxa_only <- dplyr::select(stations, starts_with("tax"))
cluster_workflow <- workflow(
  recipe(~ ., data = taxa_only) |>
    step_log(all_numeric_predictors(), offset = 1) |>
    step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()),
  k_means(num_clusters = 2) |> set_engine("stats", nstart = 25, iter.max = 100))

fit_clusters <- \(data) fit(cluster_workflow, dplyr::select(data, starts_with("tax")))
assign_clusters <- \(fitted, data) predict(fitted, data)$.pred_cluster

set.seed(41)
habitat_fit <- fit_clusters(stations)
original <- assign_clusters(habitat_fit, stations)

set.seed(12)
resamples <- group_bootstraps(stations, group = site_id, times = 60)
replicates <- map_dfr(resamples$splits, \(split) {
  assigned <- assign_clusters(fit_clusters(analysis(split)), stations)
  tibble(agreement = adjustedRandIndex(assigned, original),
         seabed = adjustedRandIndex(assigned, stations$bottom),
         depth_gap = abs(diff(tapply(stations$depth_m, assigned, median))))
})

replicates |>
  mutate(outcome = if_else(agreement > 0.5, "same as original", "different")) |>
  summarise(samples = n(),
            `ARI with original` = round(mean(agreement), 2),
            `ARI with seabed` = round(mean(seabed), 2),
            `depth between clusters (m)` = round(mean(depth_gap)),
            .by = outcome)
```

## Python

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.base import clone
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import adjusted_rand_score
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import FunctionTransformer, StandardScaler

from mlbasic_data import load_coastal_community, load_coastal_survey_clean

survey = load_coastal_survey_clean()
community = load_coastal_community()

stations = community.merge(
    survey[["station_id", "site_id", "depth_m", "substrate"]], on="station_id")
stations["bottom"] = np.where(stations["substrate"].isin(["rock", "gravel"]),
                              "hard", "soft")

cluster_workflow = Pipeline([
    ("log", FunctionTransformer(np.log1p, feature_names_out="one-to-one")),
    ("normalise", StandardScaler()),
    ("model", KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=25, max_iter=100, random_state=41)),
])

def fit_clusters(data):
    return clone(cluster_workflow).fit(data.filter(like="tax"))

def assign_clusters(fitted, data):
    return fitted.predict(data.filter(like="tax")) + 1

# scikit-learn has no group bootstrap: draw sites with replacement and
# take every station of each site drawn.
def site_bootstrap(data, rng):
    sites = data["site_id"].unique()
    drawn = rng.choice(sites, size=len(sites), replace=True)
    return pd.concat([data[data["site_id"] == site] for site in drawn])

habitat_fit = fit_clusters(stations)
original = assign_clusters(habitat_fit, stations)

rng = np.random.default_rng(12)
rows = []
for sample in range(60):
    assigned = assign_clusters(fit_clusters(site_bootstrap(stations, rng)), stations)
    medians = stations.groupby(assigned)["depth_m"].median()
    rows.append({"agreement": adjusted_rand_score(assigned, original),
                 "seabed": adjusted_rand_score(assigned, stations["bottom"]),
                 "depth_gap": abs(medians.iloc[1] - medians.iloc[0])})
replicates = pd.DataFrame(rows)

outcome = np.where(replicates["agreement"] > 0.5, "same as original", "different")
(replicates.groupby(outcome, sort=False)
    .agg(samples=("agreement", "size"),
         ari_original=("agreement", "mean"),
         ari_seabed=("seabed", "mean"),
         depth_gap=("depth_gap", "mean"))
    .round({"ari_original": 2, "ari_seabed": 2, "depth_gap": 0})
    .rename(columns={"ari_original": "ARI with original",
                     "ari_seabed": "ARI with seabed",
                     "depth_gap": "depth between clusters (m)"})
    .rename_axis("outcome")
    .reset_index())
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-numbers
#| include: false
same <- filter(replicates, agreement > 0.5)
different <- filter(replicates, agreement <= 0.5)
```

In `r nrow(same)` of the 60 samples the original grouping comes back almost exactly, with
an average ARI of `r round(mean(same$agreement), 2)`: hard bottom against soft. The other
`r nrow(different)` give a grouping with almost nothing in common with it. Their clusters
barely follow the seabed, with an ARI of `r round(mean(different$seabed), 2)`, and sit
`r round(mean(different$depth_gap))` m apart in median depth against
`r round(mean(same$depth_gap))` m: they split the survey into shallow and deep.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: fig-bootstrap
#| fig-cap: "Agreement between each of 60 bootstrap refits and the original grouping. The refits give one of two answers, and nothing in between; the dashed line, the average, falls where no refit landed."
#| fig-alt: !expr 'glue::glue("Histogram of the adjusted Rand index with the original grouping for 60 bootstrap refits, on an axis from 0 to 1. {nrow(different)} refits form a short bar near {round(mean(different$agreement), 1)} at the far left and {nrow(same)} form a tall bar near 1 at the far right; the range between is empty. A dashed vertical line marks the average, {round(mean(replicates$agreement), 2)}, in the empty range just left of the tall bar.")'
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(replicates, aes(agreement)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = ml_palette[["blue"]],
                 colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(replicates$agreement), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = ml_palette[["vermilion"]], linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = mean(replicates$agreement) - 0.02, y = 0.75 * nrow(same),
           hjust = 1, label = "average", colour = ml_palette[["vermilion"]],
           size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "ARI with the original grouping", y = "bootstrap samples")
```

:::

The average ARI is `r round(mean(replicates$agreement), 2)`, which reads like one stable
answer with some noise, but no refit came near it. The data holds two competing
two-cluster answers, and the seabed split is the stronger: it came back
`r nrow(same)` times out of 60. Report how often each answer came back, not the average.

### A soft-bottom split comes back every time but has no gap

Now the soft-bottom stations alone, where the seabed leaves no boundary to find. k-means
splits them into two clusters as readily, and the bootstrap check is repeated on them.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: soft-bottom
soft <- filter(stations, bottom == "soft")

set.seed(41)
soft_fit <- fit_clusters(soft)
soft_original <- assign_clusters(soft_fit, soft)

set.seed(14)
soft_resamples <- group_bootstraps(soft, group = site_id, times = 60)
soft_agreement <- map_dbl(soft_resamples$splits, \(split)
  adjustedRandIndex(assign_clusters(fit_clusters(analysis(split)), soft),
                    soft_original))

depths <- tapply(soft$depth_m, soft_original, median)
tibble(`median depth, cluster 1 (m)` = round(depths[[1]]),
       `median depth, cluster 2 (m)` = round(depths[[2]]),
       `lowest ARI with original` = round(min(soft_agreement), 2),
       `average ARI with original` = round(mean(soft_agreement), 2))
```

## Python

```{python}
soft = stations[stations["bottom"] == "soft"].reset_index(drop=True)

soft_fit = fit_clusters(soft)
soft_original = assign_clusters(soft_fit, soft)

picker = np.random.default_rng(14)
soft_agreement = np.array([
    adjusted_rand_score(
        assign_clusters(fit_clusters(site_bootstrap(soft, picker)), soft),
        soft_original)
    for sample in range(60)
])

depths = soft.groupby(soft_original)["depth_m"].median()
pd.DataFrame([{
    "median depth, cluster 1 (m)": round(depths[1]),
    "median depth, cluster 2 (m)": round(depths[2]),
    "lowest ARI with original": round(soft_agreement.min(), 2),
    "average ARI with original": round(soft_agreement.mean(), 2),
}])
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: soft-numbers
#| include: false
soft_depths <- sort(tapply(soft$depth_m, soft_original, median))
```

This split never fails the way the seabed split did: every refit agrees with it at an ARI
of `r round(min(soft_agreement), 2)` or more, and none gives a different answer. It divides the soft bottom into a shallow
cluster, with a median depth of `r round(soft_depths[[1]])` m, and a deep one at
`r round(soft_depths[[2]])` m. By the first check alone, it would be reported as two
soft-bottom assemblages.

The second check asks whether the two clusters are separated by a gap. Each station gets
a position on the straight line from the first cluster centre to the second, 0 at the
first and 1 at the second, measured in the logged, standardised counts the clustering used.
The boundary between the clusters is half way. Groups leave few stations near the
boundary; a gradient leaves as many there as anywhere.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: positions
# Where each station sits on the line from centre 1 (0) to centre 2 (1).
position_between_centres <- function(fitted, data) {
  scaled <- bake(extract_recipe(fitted),
                 new_data = dplyr::select(data, starts_with("tax"))) |>
    as.matrix()
  centres <- extract_fit_engine(fitted)$centers
  direction <- centres[2, ] - centres[1, ]
  offset <- sweep(scaled[, colnames(centres)], 2, centres[1, ])
  drop(offset %*% direction) / sum(direction^2)
}

positions <- bind_rows(
  tibble(split = "All stations, two clusters",
         position = position_between_centres(habitat_fit, stations)),
  tibble(split = "Soft bottom only, two clusters",
         position = position_between_centres(soft_fit, soft),
         depth_m = soft$depth_m))

positions |>
  summarise(stations = n(),
            `share within 0.1 of the boundary` =
              round(mean(abs(position - 0.5) < 0.1), 3),
            .by = split)
```

## Python

```{python}
def position_between_centres(fitted, data):
    scaled = fitted[:-1].transform(data.filter(like="tax"))
    centres = fitted["model"].cluster_centers_
    direction = centres[1] - centres[0]
    return (scaled - centres[0]) @ direction / (direction @ direction)

positions = pd.concat([
    pd.DataFrame({"split": "All stations, two clusters",
                  "position": position_between_centres(habitat_fit, stations)}),
    pd.DataFrame({"split": "Soft bottom only, two clusters",
                  "position": position_between_centres(soft_fit, soft),
                  "depth_m": soft["depth_m"]}),
])

(positions.groupby("split")["position"]
    .agg(stations="size",
         near_boundary=lambda p: round((abs(p - 0.5) < 0.1).mean(), 3))
    .rename(columns={"near_boundary": "share within 0.1 of the boundary"})
    .reset_index())
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: position-numbers
#| include: false
near <- positions |>
  summarise(share = mean(abs(position - 0.5) < 0.1), .by = split) |>
  pull(share)
soft_positions <- filter(positions, !is.na(depth_m))
depth_cor <- abs(cor(soft_positions$position, soft_positions$depth_m))
soft_taxa <- load_coastal_community_taxa() |> filter(group == "soft-substrate")
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: fig-positions
#| fig-cap: "Where each station sits between the two cluster centres, 0 at one centre and 1 at the other; the dashed line is the boundary between the clusters. The seabed split leaves a gap at the boundary; the soft-bottom split cuts through the middle of one broad spread."
#| fig-alt: !expr 'glue::glue("Two histograms of position between the two cluster centres, from about minus 0.5 to 1.5, with a dashed vertical line at 0.5. Top, all stations: a low, wide hump around 0 and a tall hump around 1, with a dip almost to zero at 0.5, where {scales::percent(near[1], accuracy = 1)} of stations lie within 0.1 of the boundary. Bottom, soft bottom only: one broad spread from about minus 0.4 to 1.4, with bars running straight across the boundary and no dip, {scales::percent(near[2], accuracy = 1)} of stations within 0.1 of the boundary.")'
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.6
ggplot(positions, aes(position)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = ml_palette[["blue"]],
                 colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = ml_palette[["vermilion"]], linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ split, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "position between the two cluster centres", y = "stations")
```

:::

The seabed split has a gap: only `r scales::percent(near[1], accuracy = 1)` of stations
lie within 0.1 of its boundary. The soft-bottom split has none:
`r scales::percent(near[2], accuracy = 1)` of its stations lie that close, about
`r round(near[2] / near[1])` times as many. The soft-bottom stations run in one continuous
line from one centre to the other, and k-means cut the line in the middle. It cuts near
the same middle in every bootstrap sample, which is why the split comes back.

Depth, which the clustering was never given, shows what the line is. A station's position
correlates `r round(depth_cor, 2)` with its depth: the soft-bottom communities change
steadily from shallow to deep. The simulation behind the survey agrees, since it gave the
`r nrow(soft_taxa)` soft-bottom taxa depth optima spread from
`r min(soft_taxa$depth_optimum_m)` to `r max(soft_taxa$depth_optimum_m)` m with no break
between them.

### Only the seabed split matches a recorded category

The last check compares each grouping with recorded variables: the seabed, and depth cut
into three bands of equal size. For the soft-bottom split, the seabed is sand against mud.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: external
depth_band <- cut(stations$depth_m,
                  breaks = quantile(stations$depth_m, c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)),
                  include.lowest = TRUE)
soft_band <- depth_band[stations$bottom == "soft"]

external <- tibble(
  split = c("All stations", "Soft bottom only"),
  `ARI with recorded seabed` = c(adjustedRandIndex(original, stations$bottom),
                                 adjustedRandIndex(soft_original, soft$substrate)),
  `ARI with depth band` = c(adjustedRandIndex(original, depth_band),
                            adjustedRandIndex(soft_original, soft_band)))
external |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Python

```{python}
depth_band = pd.qcut(stations["depth_m"], q=3)
soft_band = depth_band[(stations["bottom"] == "soft").to_numpy()]

external = pd.DataFrame({
    "split": ["All stations", "Soft bottom only"],
    "ARI with recorded seabed": [
        adjusted_rand_score(original, stations["bottom"]),
        adjusted_rand_score(soft_original, soft["substrate"])],
    "ARI with depth band": [
        adjusted_rand_score(original, depth_band),
        adjusted_rand_score(soft_original, soft_band)],
})
external.round(2)
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: external-numbers
#| include: false
ext <- external |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

The seabed split matches the recorded seabed at an ARI of
`r ext[[2]][1]` and depth bands at `r ext[[3]][1]`: from the counts alone, k-means found a
category it was never shown. The soft-bottom split matches sand and mud at
`r ext[[2]][2]` and depth bands at `r ext[[3]][2]`.

Agreement with a recorded **category**, such as the seabed, is evidence of groups.
Agreement with a **continuous** variable cut into bands is not: cutting a gradient into
two clusters and depth into three bands gives part agreement whether or not groups exist.
What it shows is a gradient, and a gradient is a finding too.

The three checks together give a result that can be reported: the communities form two
groups, hard and soft bottom, found in `r nrow(same)` of 60 bootstrap samples and matching
the recorded seabed at an ARI of `r ext[[2]][1]`; within the soft bottom, composition
changes steadily with depth, with no boundary.

## A checked pattern is still a hypothesis

The checks show whether a pattern in this survey is worth reporting, not that it holds
elsewhere. Treat it as a hypothesis for the next survey, or for a supervised model to test
on new data.

## Key points

::: {.key-points}
- Check three things before reporting a cluster: does it come back in **bootstrap
  samples**, is it a **group or a cut through a gradient**, and does it match a
  **recorded variable** the method never saw.
- Draw whole sites in the bootstrap when stations at one site are alike. Report how often
  each answer came back: here `r nrow(same)` of 60 samples gave the seabed split and
  `r nrow(different)` a depth split, and the average ARI described neither.
- **Coming back is not enough.** A split through a steady gradient falls in the same place
  every time: no bootstrap sample of the soft bottom gave a different answer.
- Groups leave a **gap** at the boundary between their centres; a gradient leaves
  stations all along it.
- Agreement with a recorded **category** is evidence of groups. Agreement with a
  continuous variable cut into bands shows a gradient, which is a finding in its own
  right.
:::

## Try it yourself

1. Replace `group_bootstraps(stations, group = site_id, times = 60)` with
   `bootstraps(stations, times = 60)`, which draws single stations. How many samples now
   give the depth split, and why might drawing stations make the result look surer than
   it is?
2. Repeat the bootstrap check with `num_clusters = 3`. Do the refits still give two
   competing answers, and what does the third cluster follow?
